key_insight: Active learning makes machine learning interatomic potentials far more data-efficient by iteratively choosing the most informative configurations instead of training only on predefined datasets.
engineering_relevance: This enables more reliable atomistic simulation and materials design for specific target conditions, from mechanics and diffusion to reactive chemistry and functional materials.
method: Loop: generate candidates -> estimate uncertainty -> select new data -> run reference calculations -> update the model
Uses approaches such as on-the-fly molecular dynamics, query-by-committee, Gaussian process force fields, and pretrained-model fine-tuning
Extends to kernel/representation-based acquisition and reaction-aware sampling for systems far from equilibrium
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes more than seventy studies, with emphasis on 2020-2026 work across diverse materials and chemistry applications.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are not directly comparable across model architectures and can be least reliable in the exact regions where active learning depends on them most.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
